message.content:
Write high-intent SEO landing pages for the Nxeon VPS host (Next.js App Router, /opt/nxeon). FIRST read the exemplar `/opt/nxeon/app/(marketing)/wordpress-vps-hosting/page.tsx` and the template `/opt/nxeon/components/marketing/UseCaseLanding.tsx` — copy that EXACT structure and quality. Each page is a server component that fetches `db.plan.findMany({ where: { active: true }, orderBy: { sortOrder: "asc" } })` and renders `<UseCaseLanding content={content} plans={plans} />` with a full `UseCaseContent` object and `export const metadata` + `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`.

Create these files (each a NEW directory under app/(marketing)/):
1. app/(marketing)/docker-hosting/page.tsx — "Docker hosting / Docker VPS"
2. app/(marketing)/n8n-hosting/page.tsx — "n8n hosting / self-hosted n8n automation"
3. app/(marketing)/nodejs-hosting/page.tsx — "Node.js VPS hosting"
4. app/(marketing)/nextcloud-hosting/page.tsx — "Nextcloud hosting / self-hosted cloud storage"

STRICT ACCURACY — only claim what's true (never invent features/prices):
- Plans (real, from db): Nano $6.49 (1 vCPU/1GB/15GB/1TB), Starter $8.99 (1/2GB/25GB/1TB), Standard $12.99 (2/4GB/50GB/2TB), Pro $20.99 (3/8GB/80GB/4TB), Max $32.99 (4/16GB/120GB/8TB). Intro % off first term, renews at regular price. PricingGrid renders these; don't restate all prices in prose beyond "from $6.49/mo".
- Real features: enterprise NVMe SSD on a self-healing ZFS mirror; full root via SSH; dedicated IPv4 included; always-on DDoS protection + managed firewall; automatic daily backups; instant snapshots; noVNC web console; one-click resize of vCPU/RAM/disk with no rebuild; IPv6 ready; 2FA (TOTP); SSH key management; real-time metrics; ~47s median deploy; 99.9% uptime SLA; no credit card to sign up.
- One-click images available: Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, AlmaLinux 9, Rocky 9; apps: Docker, WordPress, Nextcloud, Ghost, n8n, PostgreSQL. Docker and n8n and Nextcloud ARE one-click apps — say so. Node.js is NOT a one-click app (deploy on Ubuntu/Debian and install Node/nvm, or run in Docker) — be honest.
- Single datacenter: Singapore (low-latency for Asia-Pacific). Do NOT imply multiple regions.
- CTAs go to /register and /pricing. Internal `related` links should point to real pages: /vps, /pricing, /tools, /docker-hosting, /wordpress-vps-hosting, /game-servers, and each other.

Per page write GENUINELY UNIQUE content (not boilerplate): a specific 2-3 paragraph intro about hosting THAT app on a VPS, 6 "why" cards tailored to it, 3-4 concrete deploy steps, a specNote sizing hint (e.g. n8n runs fine on 2GB Starter; Nextcloud wants more disk/RAM as it grows), and 5 real FAQs. Match the exemplar's tone. metadata title ~55-60 chars, description ~150 chars, canonical set to the slug.

Do NOT edit any shared files (sitemap, footer, header) — I handle integration. Only create the 4 new page files. When done, report the list of files created and any per-page notes.

This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files.
